items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the social services law, in relation to directing the council on children and families to establish an online listing and map of publicly funded or registered afterschool and school age child care programs
items.lawCode: Amd §§483-g, add 17 & 2, Soc Serv L; amd §305, Ed L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S6553

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the social services law, in relation
to directing the council on children and families to establish an
online listing and map of publicly funded or registered afterschool
and school age child care programs

PURPOSE:

This bill ensures the Council on Children and Families develops and
makes available through its website a listing and map of all
recipients of grants awarded or administered by the state for the
purpose of providing afterschool or summer programs, extended learning
time, or community schools, and all registered school age providers
registered by the office of children and family services.  The listing
shall include for each grant recipient or provider the recipient or
provider's name, the address at which the program is offered, and the
name and phone number of an individual who is authorized to answer
questions regarding the program.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 483-b of the social services law by adding a
new subdivision 6 that requires the Council on Children and Families
to develop and make available through its website a listing and map of
all recipients of grants awarded or administered by the state for the
purpose of providing afterschool or summer programs, extended learning
time, or community schools, and all registered school age providers
registered by the office of children and family services.  The listing
shall include each grant recipient or provider's name, the address at
which the program is offered, and the name and phone number of an
individual who is authorized to answer questions regarding the
program. The listing and map shall be updated no less than once every
ninety days to reflect changes. The listing and map shall be updated
within ninety days of any contract with a grant recipient expiring or
being signed. The council may include locations and information for
additional relevant programs as it sees fit.

Section 2 establishes the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

As it stands now, there is no statewide database through which parents
and caregivers can search to identify afterschool, extended learning,
and summer programs for their school age children. This bill will
begin to address this gap in information and services.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined

EFFECTIVE DATE:


This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S6553A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the social services law, in relation
to directing the council on children and families to establish an
online listing and map of publicly funded or registered afterschool
and school age childcare programs and to expand the duties of the
commissioner of social services; and to amend the education law, in
relation to expanding the duties of the commissioner of education

PURPOSE:  This bill ensures the Council on Children and Families
develops and makes available through its website a listing and map of
all recipients of grants awarded or administered by the state for the
purpose of providing afterschool or summer programs, extended learning
time, or community schools, and all registered school age providers
registered by the office of children and family services.  The listing
shall include for each grant recipient or provider the recipient or
provider's name, the address at which the program is offered, and the
name and phone number of an individual who is authorized to answer
questions regarding the program.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends social service law by adding section 483-g that
requires the Council on Children and Families to develop and make
available through its website a listing and map of all recipients of
competitive grants awarded or administered by the state included but
not limited to grants under section 3641 of the education law, grants
awarded or administered by the state for the purpose of providing
afterschool or summer programs, extended learning time, or community
schools, and all registered school age providers registered by the
office of children and family services. The listing shall include each
grant recipient or provider's name, the address at which the program
is offered, and the name and phone number of an individual who is
authorized to answer questions regarding the program. The listing and
map shall be updated no less than once every ninety days to reflect
changes. The listing and map shall be updated within ninety days of
any contract with a grant recipient expiring or being signed. The
council may include locations and information for additional relevant
programs as it sees fit.

Section 2 amends subdivisions (h) and (i) of section 17 of the social
services law to require that the Commissioner of Children and Families
Services make available to the Council on Children and Families,
through the OpenNY website, information regarding all recipients of
grants awarded or administered by the state for the purposes of
providing afterschool or summer programs as defined in section two of
this chapter, extended learning time, including but not limited to
grants for such purposes awarded under section thirty-six hundred
forty-one of the education law, and registered school age child care
providers registered by the office of children and family services.
For each grant recipient or provider, information concerning name, the
address at which the program is offered, and the name and phone number
of an individual who is authorized to answer questions regarding the
program will be made available through the OpenNY website no less than
once a year and within 90 days of the date of execution or expiration
of contracts with grant recipients when all such contracts are
executing or expiring for a particular competitive grant.


Section 3 amends section 305 of the education law by adding a new
subdivision 52 to require the Commissioner of Children and Family
Services to provide the council information regarding all recipients
of grants for afterschool, summer programs, or extended learning time
awarded or administered by the state , including but not limited to
grants for such purposes awarded under section 3641 of this chapter,
or community schools. Each grant recipient's name, address and contact
information for a person authorized to answer questions regarding the
program. The information must be provided to the council no less than
once a year and within 90 days of the date of the execution and
expiration of grant with grant recipients.

Section 4 defines "afterschool program" and "summer program"

Section 5 establishes the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:  As it stands now, there is no statewide database
through which parents and caregivers can search to identify
afterschool, extended learning, and summer programs for their school
age children. This bill will begin to address this gap in information
and services.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: None

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: To be determined

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after
it shall have become a law.
